catalog_quote: Central to the analysis is the minimal phonological word, a binary constituent known as a couplet in traditional studies of Mixtec. The couplet normally consists of a root having one of the following shapes: CVCV, CVV, VCV, VV. Stress is on the first (C)V. Since there are no couplets of the shape CVVCV or CVCCV ... there is some indeterminacy about whether the couplet should be referred to as consisting of two moras or two syllables. The couplet may be preceded or followed by monosyllabic morphemes which are dependent on the root. In this study, we shall refer to those which precede the root as proclitics and those which follow the root as enclitics. ... Perhaps the most intriguing feature of the above analysis concerns the status of L tone, which can only be realized on the first (stressed) syllable of a couplet ... Since all trisyllabic words are analyzable as morphologically complex,…

new_statements.quote: p.19: "El acento se localiza en la penúltima sílaba de los morfemas de dos o más sílabas. (La dependencia fonológica de los morfemas de una sola sílaba se indica con un guion (-) que se coloca antes de los enclíticos y después de los proclíticos.) Los morfemas que consisten en una sílaba tienen la forma canónica V y CV." p.20: "La mayor parte de los morfemas constan de una o dos sílabas, pero unos cuantos constan de tres sílabas." p.25: "Las vocales se alargan optativamente en sílaba acentuada. Como alternativa, la consonante que sigue a la vocal se alarga, o se alargan la vocal y la consonante. /kiši-dé/ [kiši-dé] ~ [kiˑši-dé] 'venir él'"
new_statements.translation: p.19: "Stress is located on the penultimate syllable of morphemes of two or more syllables. (The phonological dependence of one-syllable morphemes is indicated with a hyphen (-) placed before enclitics and after proclitics.) Morphemes consisting of one syllable have the canonical shape V and CV." p.20: "Most morphemes consist of one or two syllables, but a few consist of three syllables." p.25: "Vowels are optionally lengthened in the stressed syllable. Alternatively, the consonant following the vowel is lengthened, or both the vowel and the consonant are lengthened. /kiši-dé/ [kiši-dé] ~ [kiˑši-dé] 'he comes'"

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Peñoles Mixtec (catalog-all-2026-09-12) has an empty rule and there are no existing stress statements, so this source supplies the placement outright: penultimate syllable of the (mostly disyllabic) morpheme, tonal language, optional stressed-syllable lengthening. It contradicts nothing.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (acento) falls on the penultimate syllable of every morpheme of two or more syllables; since most stems are disyllabic (the Mixtec couplet) this is the first syllable of the stem. Monosyllabic morphemes are clitics (written with a hyphen) and carry no stress of their own. The stressed syllable may optionally be realized with a lengthened vowel and/or lengthened following consonant. The language is tonal (high and low tones, plus modified high and low tones, p.25ff.), so stress is a separate, predictable property alongside lexical tone.
new_statements.exceptions: No exceptions stated. Trisyllabic morphemes exist (a few, loans or native, e.g. /andiu/ 'cielo', /ʃikwela/ 'escuela'); the penultimate rule covers them without comment. The domain is the morpheme, not the phonological word: stem + enclitic sequences such as /kiši-dé/ keep stress on the stem's penult.
new_statements.identity_note: All material concerns the Mixtec of Santa María Peñoles, Oaxaca (ISO mil, Glottolog peno1244), the variety John and Margaret Daly worked on; the ALIM 3 volume names the town explicitly in its title. No other dialect is described.
